# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Puzzles where the primary goal is placing numbers into cells according to constraints*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Digit Exclusion
- **Sudoku** — Place digits 1–9 with no repeats in rows, columns, or boxes
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill regions with numbers; identical numbers must be separated by distance equal to their value
- **Makaro** — Fill regions with digits 1–N; arrows in cells indicate the largest neighbor

### 1.2 Number-Region Relationship
- **Nansuke** — Numbers indicate properties of their enclosing regions
- **Kurodoko** — Place black cells; white numbered cells see exactly that many white cells in their row/column
- **Usowan** — Like Heyawake but exactly one clue per row is a "liar"

---

## 2. REGION DIVISION / AREA PARTITION PUZZLES
*Puzzles where the grid must be divided into contiguous regions satisfying given constraints*

### 2.1 Fixed-Shape Regions
- **Shikaku** — Divide the grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Sashigane** — Divide the grid into L-shaped trominoes (or similar L-shapes)
- **Five Cells** — Divide the grid into pentomino-shaped regions of exactly five cells

### 2.2 Polyomino / Free-Form Regions
- **Fillomino** — Divide the grid into polyominoes; numbers indicate region size; same-size regions may not touch
- **Double Choco** — Divide the grid into regions each consisting of two congruent halves (one shaded, one not)
- **Evolomino** — Divide into regions where each region "evolves" from another by defined transformation rules
- **LITS** — Shade one tetromino per region; shaded tetrominoes connect, no 2×2 block, same-shape tetrominoes don't touch

### 2.3 Number-Constrained Regions
- **Nurikabe** — Shade cells so white islands match numbered clues; no 2×2 shaded blocks; all shading connected
- **Kurotto** — Shade cells; numbers in circles indicate total size of connected shaded groups touching them
- **Choco Banana** — Divide into rectangles; shade some; numbered clues constrain size/shape of shaded rectangles

---

## 3. CELL SHADING PUZZLES
*Puzzles primarily involving deciding which cells to shade or leave unshaded*

### 3.1 Connectivity-Based Shading
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in a row/column; shaded cells don't touch; unshaded cells connected
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells; no 2×2 shaded; no unshaded run crosses more than one region boundary; numbered rooms have fixed shaded count
- **Norinori** — Shade exactly two cells per region; every shaded cell shares an edge with exactly one other shaded cell
- **Nuritwin** — Shade cells so shaded regions appear in congruent pairs
- **Tilepaint** — Shade entire rectangular tiles; clues constrain which tiles are shaded

### 3.2 Shape / Geometry Shading
- **Shakashaka** — Place right triangles in cells; all unshaded space forms rectangles
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells; each unshaded connected group has exactly one "cape" cell (touching shading on three sides); numbered capes indicate group size
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade cells to form a maze-like path structure satisfying connectivity constraints
- **Kurodoko** *(also listed under 1.2)*

### 3.3 Symbolic / Pattern Shading
- **Sto-stone** — Place one or two stones per region; stones fall downward; each column's stone count equals a given number

---

## 4. PATH & LOOP PUZZLES
*Puzzles involving drawing a single or multiple continuous paths or closed loops*

### 4.1 Single Closed Loop
- **Slitherlink** — Draw a single closed loop along grid edges; numbers indicate how many sides of each cell are used
- **Masyu** — Draw a closed loop through circles; black circles force a turn; white circles force straight passage
- **Yajilin** — Draw a closed loop; shade some cells; arrows/numbers indicate shaded cells in that direction
- **Mid-loop** — Draw a closed loop that passes through the midpoint of certain edges per given constraints

### 4.2 Open Paths / Branching Paths
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching numbered pairs with non-crossing paths that fill the entire grid
- **Pencils** — Draw straight-line pencil strokes from clue cells; strokes fill the grid without overlap
- **Hebi** — Draw snake-shaped paths through the grid satisfying length and directional constraints
- **Nagareru** — Draw paths that "flow" through the grid following current/directional constraints
- **Suraromu** — Draw paths around or through regions satisfying given turning/length rules

### 4.3 Multi-Path / Special Loop Variants
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Draw loops through cells; each cell with a clue indicates which of two loop options applies
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Draw a loop passing through moon and sun symbols; regions alternate moon-dominated and sun-dominated
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect island circles with bridges (1 or 2 per pair); all islands connected; bridges don't cross

---

## 5. OBJECT PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Puzzles involving placing discrete objects (lights, stones, symbols) onto the grid*

### 5.1 Illumination / Visibility
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs so every cell is lit; bulbs don't illuminate each other; numbered black cells have exact bulb count among neighbors

### 5.2 Movement / Gravity
- **Yosenabe** — Slide numbered pieces toward target cells; total values meeting at each target satisfy given constraints
- **Satogaeri** — Return circles to their home regions by sliding; each region receives exactly one circle; paths don't cross
- **Chained Block** — Slide or chain blocks across the grid to satisfy connectivity or positional constraints

### 5.3 Flow / Assignment
- **Juosan** — Draw horizontal or vertical lines in each cell; lines in the same row/column of a region must all be the same orientation

---

## 6. HYBRID / COMPOSITE PUZZLES
*Puzzles that combine two or more primary mechanics (shading + path, region + number, etc.)*

| Puzzle | Primary Mechanic A | Primary Mechanic B |
|---|---|---|
| **Kurodoko** | Cell shading | Visibility/number |
| **Heyawake** | Cell shading | Region division |
| **Yajilin** | Loop drawing | Cell shading |
| **LITS** | Region division | Polyomino shading |
| **Norinori** | Cell shading | Pairing constraint |
| **Usowan** | Cell shading | Number placement |
| **Double Choco** | Region division | Shading symmetry |
| **Sto-stone** | Object placement | Gravity/shading |

---

## SUMMARY TREE

```
Grid-Based Logic Puzzles
├── 1. Number Placement
│   ├── 1.1 Latin Square / Digit Exclusion (Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro)
│   └── 1.2 Number-Region Relationship (Nansuke, Kurodoko, Usowan)
├── 2. Region Division / Area Partition
│   ├── 2.1 Fixed-Shape Regions (Shikaku, Sashigane, Five Cells)
│   ├── 2.2 Polyomino / Free-Form Regions (Fillomino, Double Choco, Evolomino, LITS)
│   └── 2.3 Number-Constrained Regions (Nurikabe, Kurotto, Choco Banana)
├── 3. Cell Shading
│   ├── 3.1 Connectivity-Based (Hitori, Heyawake, Norinori, Nuritwin, Tilepaint)
│   ├── 3.2 Shape/Geometry (Shakashaka, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu)
│   └── 3.3 Symbolic/Pattern (Sto-stone)
├── 4. Path & Loop
│   ├── 4.1 Single Closed Loop (Slitherlink, Masyu, Yajilin, Mid-loop)
│   ├── 4.2 Open / Branching Paths (Numberlink, Pencils, Hebi, Nagareru, Suraromu)
│   └── 4.3 Multi-Path / Special Variants (Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Hashiwokakero)
├── 5. Object Placement
│   ├── 5.1 Illumination / Visibility (Akari)
│   ├── 5.2 Movement / Gravity (Yosenabe, Satogaeri, Chained Block)
│   └── 5.3 Flow / Assignment (Juosan)
└── 6. Hybrid / Composite (cross-cutting entries)
```

---

> **Note on Classification:** Several puzzles could reasonably appear in more than one category. Cross-listed entries (e.g., *Kurodoko*, *Yajilin*, *LITS*) are placed in their *most dominant* mechanic category and flagged in the Hybrid section. Classifications reflect the **primary solving mechanic** rather than surface presentation.
